notes: Check batch 2026-10-23-check-3 for order-report: four skill runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, so opus is unavailable in per_rule. All four have rc 0 and model_id matching their tier; each result.json records head 4215aa3 with uncommitted changes and skill_hash d31ff0b2..., which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the current idiomatic-elixir/ folder, and every transcript contains the new rule's heading text. All four read SKILL.md only, so Expected reads (none) is met in all four. In the scratch folder all four pass mix format --check-formatted and run against the stand-in Decimal from the previous sweep's grading. A probe gave correct per-currency totals, last-order dates (a -02:00 order at 23:30 falls on the next UTC day in all four), empty results for [] and {:error, ...} for a missing key, a bad amount, an unknown status and a bad date. Haiku-1's top_customers keeps customers with zero completed orders ({"b", 0} in the probe), and haiku-2 reports a row missing a key as {:invalid_row, 1, :invalid_row}; no rule in the list covers these, so they are noted in the summaries only.

New rule: "Break a `->` clause whose pattern and body together pass 70 characters" (uncommitted in SKILL.md; git diff d04061d -- idiomatic-elixir/ shows only this addition, so every other listed rule is unchanged and graded to the previous sweep's standard). The deciding sentence is "A clause of `case`, `cond`, `with ... else` or `receive` stays on one line while its pattern, the `->` and its body together fit in 70 characters, not counting indentation." Every one-line clause was measured after its indentation: haiku-1 12 clauses in 5 cases, longest 66 (line 86); haiku-2 9 in 4, longest 69 (line 63); sonnet-1 12 in 5, longest 60 (line 167); sonnet-2 12 in 5, longest exactly 70 (line 135, {:error, reason} -> {:halt, {:error, {:invalid_order, index, reason}}}), which fits in 70 and so stays on one line. No clause in any run is over 70, no run broke any clause, so the layout sentence (every clause broken, blank lines between) has no case to apply to; no run wrote cond, receive or with ... else. The one-line fn arguments (fn {customer_id, summary} -> ... and similar) are outside the rule and were not counted. Runs violating the rule: 0 of 4. Runs exercising it: 4 of 4. Two runs sit at 69 and 70 characters, so the margin is thin; both are the reduce_while halt clause that wraps a row error with its position.

Unchanged rules, same standard as the previous sweep. The with rule is decided by "Count the `<-` clauses before writing `with`.": build/1's single parse call is a case in all four (haiku-1 48, haiku-2 51, sonnet-1 54, sonnet-2 82); the withs have eight (haiku-1, sonnet-1, sonnet-2) or three steps (haiku-2), with no else. The Enum/Map rule: 0 of 4; all group with Enum.group_by then Map.new; sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 count with frequencies_by while the Haiku runs take length/1 of the filtered list that also feeds the totals, held clean as before; the Decimal sums with Enum.reduce are reductions no table row replaces. Lists: haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 prepend without reversing, held clean as before because nothing downstream depends on the order; sonnet-2 reverses once. The do: rule's mixed-function sentence is exercised only by haiku-2's parse_row/1, whose block clause is set apart by a blank line; no do: body is wrapped onto its own line. Naming, captures, dates, money, atoms and processes: all four clean. Outside the list, haiku-2's build/1 @doc has no examples (the Comments rule); the other three have doctests, every defstruct uses @enforce_keys, no case or with nests inside another, and no other violation was found. Haiku-2's multi-line parse_row/1 head binding the five required keys is held clean under the head rule because a catch-all clause follows it.
